Meeting header:
Date: 2025-01-15
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Acme Head of ML), Maria Gomez (Product), Ethan Cole (Security), Sana Patel (ML Engineer)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: (see summary field)
Topics: results, tuning, security, next steps
Action items: (see action_items)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync. Quick roll call - Jordan from Redwood, Priya joining on the SE side.
[00:07] Daniel: Hi all, Daniel here.
[00:09] Maria: Maria here.
[00:11] Ethan: Ethan on security.
[00:13] Sana: Sana, ML eng, on the call.
[00:15] Jordan: Cool, agenda - results recap, what we tuned last week, review the 24h benchmark, discuss the stability run and security open items, and align on next steps toward business case closeout.
[00:28] Priya: I'll start with the tuning summary. Last week we adjusted batching from 32 to 16 for interactive endpoints and enabled prefix KV cache for the 2 most common prompt families. We also switched to the q4_0 quant profile for the small-gen model in the pilot to reduce memory and token cost.
[00:44] Sana: Quick question, when you say prefix KV cache, is that the same as the 'KV cache' you used in the demo? I think the transcript in my notes said K V cash, haha.
[00:50] Priya: Yes, kv cache, sorry auto transcription misheard it. It's the prefix caching that keeps the context key value entries for common prefixes so we avoid recomputing. That reduced token compute for repeated templates.
[00:59] Priya: The result: average latency for shortest queries dropped from ~120ms to ~95ms, p95 from 420ms to 210ms, and p99 spikes are now around 620-700ms instead of 1.2s. Token cost per session reduced ~18%. We saw a modest drop in bleu/accuracy metrics on a small eval set, about 1.2% relative, mostly in the more verbose generations.
[01:25] Daniel: That p99 improvement is great, but we're still seeing tail spikes when the concurrent user count hits the burst threshold. Any idea why those spikes remain?
[01:32] Priya: Two causes: one is noisy neighbor compaction on the Dedicated node during autoscale events, and second is a particular prompt family that forces long contexts — the runtime is still loading KV pages in that case. We recommended enabling burst capacity (temporary extra workers) and increasing the warm pool for that route.
[01:48] Jordan: We can propose a small burst config as part of the pilot fund usage, show cost delta, and then you can decide.
[01:55] Maria: For the business case, we need numbers for cost per 1k queries with current profile vs proposed burst and with/without quant. Can you put that in the spreadsheet? The link you shared earlier (https://redwood-share.example/ACME-pilot-bench.xlsx) should be updated.
[02:12] Priya: Yes I'll update the sheet with microbench rows: baseline, q4_0, batch16, batch32, burst enabled. I already uploaded a draft, will finalize today.
[02:20] Sana: We ran the local A/B test yesterday - quality delta was within expected range but the variance increased during peak load which might explain some customer reported regressions. Not a showstopper but we want to be cautious.
[02:33] Jordan: Ethan, any security blockers on your end? I know KMS integration was one item.
[02:36] Ethan: KMS integration flow is mostly clear, but we need a short doc that maps the encryption flow end-to-end and whether Redwood retains any plaintext in logs. Also the audit log retention and SSO/SAML mapping for our RBAC. Right now we need that to present to legal.
[02:53] Jordan: Understood. We'll send the security addendum plus a short KMS flow diagram. Priya can attach the routing and audit log notes.
[02:58] Priya: Quick note on logs: the console currently shows token-level breakdown and per-route latency traces. For the pilot we can enable enhanced retention for 30 days for your team.
[03:08] Ethan: That helps. Also ask about HSM vs cloud KMS - we might need HSM-backed keys for the production roll, but for the pilot cloud KMS is fine. We'll flag when we need HSM.
[03:20] Maria: Back to success criteria — to close the business case we need: 1) 95th latency under 300ms for interactive routes during normal traffic, 2) cost per query below $0.00X (placeholder) compared to current vendor, 3) no unresolved security blockers and clear onboarding tasks, and 4) an exec summary signed off. Does that align?
[03:38] Daniel: Yup and add reliability metric: no more than 1% error rate and no more than 3 incidents during a 48hr stress window.
[03:45] Jordan: Good. So our plan: Priya will provide tuned config and updated benchmarks; Sana will run a 48hr stability run on the Dedicated pilot with the new config and attach logs; Ethan will review security notes; Jordan will get pricing and contract updates.
[03:58] Sana: On the 48hr run - any specifics on load pattern? We'll mimic peak+steady: 10k steady/day with 2x bursts for 6 hours.
[04:08] Priya: That seems fine, please capture full traces for any p99 spikes and upload. We'll correlate with the runtime metrics.
[04:14] Priya: Also noticed during last week's run that memory pressure on a worker caused GC pauses—likely from an un-quantized layer in the model variant. We recommend pre-loading weights and adjusting worker memory cap to avoid eviction.
[04:26] Sana: Ok will do. We'll try the warm preload and memory cap change.
[04:31] Daniel: One operational question: if we hit acceptable numbers, what's the timeline to move from pilot to reserved Dedicated capacity? Do you have standard lead times?
[04:38] Jordan: Typical procurement + provisioning for dedicated reserved capacity is ~4-6 weeks once the contract is signed, faster if we have an existing capacity window. For private/VPC it's longer due to networking, maybe 6-10 weeks.
[04:49] Maria: Procurement will need an SOW and a pricing table that shows 12/24 month reserved commit options.
[04:55] Jordan: We'll include that in the updated package.
[04:58] Ethan: Small note on shared artifacts — please ensure any shared links don't expose logs. Use the private redwood share link with access control.
[05:05] Jordan: Agreed. We'll use the secure share.
[05:08] Priya: Quick demo snippet — I can show the trace chart and how enabling cache avoids recompute for prefix templates. (screen description) it reduced token compute by about ~30% for the templated flows.
[05:24] Sana: That's consistent with our internal tracing.
[05:28] Daniel: Any outstanding technical risks we should call out?
[05:31] Priya: Risk summary: 1) tail latency under burst - mitigations: burst workers, warm pool, preload; 2) slight quality delta from quantization - mitigation: run targeted evals and consider q5 if available; 3) autoscale noise - mitigation: tune autoscaler thresholds and prefer scheduled scale for known events.
[05:50] Jordan: Good. Anything else from Acme?
[05:53] Maria: When can we get the exec summary? We need to present to VP next Tuesday.
[05:57] Jordan: We'll target end of day Monday (2025-01-20) for a one-pager + pricing.
[06:02] Daniel: Perfect.
[06:04] Ethan: I'll review the security doc and get back with notes by 2025-01-21.
[06:07] Jordan: Great. Any blockers on the 48hr run?
[06:10] Sana: None, we'll start today with the adjusted config and upload logs as they complete.
[06:14] Jordan: Awesome. Recap of next steps: Jordan send pricing + contract, Priya update benchmark sheet and tuned configs, Sana run 48hr stability and upload traces/logs, Ethan review security addendum + KMS notes. We'll meet again next week same time unless we need an early sync for exec prep.
[06:31] Maria: Thanks everyone.
[06:33] Jordan: Thanks, bye.
[06:35] (call ended)
